newsitem.title: UK: CBI chief says UK should keep EMU option open.
newsitem.headline: CBI chief says UK should keep EMU option open.

text.p: The British government's policy of keeping its options open over joining a single European currency is the right one, the head of Britain's top employers group said on Wednesday.

Adair Turner, director-general of the Confederation of British Industry, said keeping the option open while participating fully in European Union negotiations was right for Britain's national interest.

"Britain must be fully involved in the discussions because it might make sense for us to join, and also because we have an interest in EMU's success even if we don't join," Turner told the Society of Business Economists' annual dinner.
Turner highlighted two main potential advantages of European Economic and Monetary Union.
Firstly, it would mean the creation of a complete single market, increasing competition and benefitting consumers.
Secondly, disruptive exchange rate fluctuations would cease to plague trade within Europe.
"These advantages are not trivial and create a significant economic case for an EMU achieved at the appropriate time and under the appropriate conditions," Turner said.

But he said that for EMU to succeed, labour markets would have to develop more flexibility. "What we have, therefore, is a project which could carry significant benefits to the European economy, but also carries risks."
"Britain must, therefore, play its part fully, urging on our partners the changes required to make it a success and keeping open our option to participate in a successful project," Turner said.

He referred to a recent CBI poll, conducted with the British Chambers of Commerce, which found only seven percent of 1,600 UK companies surveyed wanted to rule out joining EMU completely. The vast majority, 71 percent, wanted to leave the option open, while 28 percent wanted to commit to entry in the first wave.
